name: Ren Alston
home: the blocks north of the port
life: “I still remember renting a mattress from a cousin for a single winter.” People around the foot of Harbor Viaduct know Ren by a small Wednesday habit. Ren pauses where the machinery overhead makes two people stand close enough to hear each other.
voice: I owed her one month and found she'd put in a little every week herself.
appearance: Ren has a smooth side part with one rebellious curl, full cheeks and a mouth that pulls slightly to one side, and a favorite piece of clothing, a long navy raincoat. It usually goes with a square of clean cloth for polishing smudges. When somebody else has the floor, Ren holds eye contact until the other person has finished.
personality: Ren always notices who paid for the last round. In a group that can be a kindness or a small tyranny, and Ren is trying to tell the difference before the bill arrives.
agenda: To thank the elder who quietly covered the shortfall.
family: Reuben Grant is Ren’s stepsibling. Ren remembers the birthdays. Reuben asks what the birthday guest would like this year. A present that was perfect at sixteen may be completely wrong at forty. They take the trouble of finding out. Asked about *Closing soup*, Reuben says, “I donated the fennel nobody bought. In the soup people asked me to grow extra.”
connections: Scout Nord. The two renters compare finding money that somebody else had quietly put aside.

reactions.situation: A family asks to come back later without explanation
reactions.response: Ren arranges a second visit without repeating the family's explanation.
